---
title: "Data protection and threat model"
---

Before the first prompt, list your data and decide what may leave your environment. An agent sends prompts and selected context to a model route. It may expose data to a provider, follow untrusted text, read too broadly, reveal credentials in shell output, or create a wrong artefact.

Use the supplied source-free synthetic panel for provider-facing work. Never send restricted SOEP rows, unpublished work, personal data, or credentials. Public availability does not mean your institution approves external processing.

Provider terms differ and change. OpenCode Zen describes zero-retention and no-training defaults with named exceptions. OpenRouter routes and other products have their own terms.

OpenAI's personal ChatGPT data controls are separate from the Codex setting for training on full environments. Check both the [general data controls](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5722486-how-do-i-opt-out-of-my-content-being-used-to-improve-model-performance) and [Codex security and data guidance](https://developers.openai.com/codex/security/). Treat Google/Antigravity settings as telemetry controls, not a confidentiality guarantee; see the [permissions documentation](https://antigravity.google/docs/cli/permissions/). Recheck these links before publication.

::: {.callout-warning}
Never "anonymise later." Minimise before the first prompt. Keep fake fixtures separate. Stop if a tool proposes an external upload or reads beyond the allowed folder.
:::
